belief: People in my town will always see me as I was.
origins: In small towns and tight communities, people remember. A teenage mistake, a divorce, an addiction, or a family scandal may be recalled for decades. Even after real change, we may feel watched for relapse and seen through an old lens.
teaches: Paul writes, “From now on we regard no one according to the flesh… Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!” The Lord says, “Do not call to mind the former things; pay no attention to the things of old. Behold, I am about to do something new.” After his conversion, Saul was feared by the church, but Barnabas stood with him. God is not limited by what people remember. While some will take time to see change, others will welcome it, and our task is to live faithfully and be patient.
self_statements: They will never forget what I did.
I will always be that person to them.
No matter how I change, they will not see it.
I cannot outlive my past here.
People never change their minds about me.
errors: Assuming I know what everyone remembers and thinks.
Predicting that no one will change their view.
Treating all townspeople as one mind.
Letting an old label stand for who I am now.
questions: Who in my town has already responded to my change with kindness?
What do I want to be known for in five years?
What can I do consistently to show the change?
Whose opinion do I weigh most, and why?
What does God see when He looks at me now?
Do I need a fresh start somewhere else, or can I stay with patience?
truth: God sees me as a new creation, and He is not limited by what others recall. Some people may take time to see my change. I can live faithfully, be patient, and look for those who welcome the new.
hw_truths: God does not call to mind the former things.
Some will see the change in time.
My identity is not their memory.
log: Each week, note one thing consistent with who you are now.
actions: Write who you are now in three sentences.
Seek out those who encourage you.
Practice letting go of the need to be fully understood.
prayer: Father, You make all things new. Free me from living under others’ memory, help me live faithfully, and give me patience while people see the change. Amen.
hw_questions: What do I want to be known for?
name_example: Sarah can write: “The old has passed away, and the new has come.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “People in my town will always see me as I was.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
